facts.text: RLBenchEnv is a Gymnasium environment: class RLBenchEnv(gym.Env)
The state observation mode disables all high-dimensional observations and enables all low-dimensional ones
The wrapper constructs the RLBench Environment headless, launches it and gets the requested task environment from it
The observation space is a Dict built from the first observation: an rgb member is a Box bounded 0 to 255 and every other member a Box bounded -inf to inf, with the observation's shape and dtype
The action space is a Box of action_mode.action_bounds() with the shape of Environment.action_shape

The extracted state observation keeps joint_velocities, joint_positions, joint_forces, gripper_open, gripper_pose, gripper_joint_positions, gripper_touch_forces and task_low_dim_state, and wraps a scalar in an array of one
reset seeds numpy's global generator, reads options['reset_to_demo'] when present, resets the task environment and returns the extracted observation with the text descriptions
step delegates to the task environment and returns (observation, reward, terminated, False, {})
The default action mode is JointPositionActionMode, which uses JointPosition(False) delta joint positions for the arm and absolute GripperJointPosition(True) for the gripper
The default action mode applies the arm and gripper targets, steps the scene once and then re-applies the post-step targets
JointPositionActionMode.action_bounds returns 7 arm deltas in [-0.1, 0.1] and one gripper value in [0.0, 0.04]
The Panda entry of SUPPORTED_ROBOTS has 7 joints
GripperJointPosition repeats the single gripper action for both joints and uses it as the absolute target
TaskEnvironment.step returns the scene observation, float(success) as the reward and the task's terminate flag
ReachTarget's task_low_dim_state is the 3-element target position
The Gymnasium ids are built at import time as rlbench/{task_name}-{obs_mode}-v0 with entry point rlbench.gym:RLBenchEnv and nondeterministic=True
Scene.step calls the PyRep simulator step and then the task step
RLBench is built around CoppeliaSim v4.1.0 and PyRep
The optional gym extra installs gymnasium==1.0.0a2

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's initial joint positions and target, and its kinematic update is deterministic; upstream seeds numpy in reset (gym.py:104) but registers every id nondeterministic=True (__init__.py:47) and was not run here, so the seed does not select the same trajectory on the two implementations

gaps: the package fake is kinematic: a tick adds the commanded arm delta to the joint positions and sets the gripper joints to the commanded absolute value; it models no contacts, collisions, dynamics, forces or physics engine, while upstream steps the CoppeliaSim scene (rlbench/backend/scene.py:314-316)

the fake was never compared with a real RLBench run: RLBench needs CoppeliaSim v4.1.0 and PyRep (README.md:64) and was not installed or imported here; the observation keys follow the upstream extract list (rlbench/gym.py:78) but every value is synthetic
no fixed physics timestep is published in the clone and the environment exposes no dt attribute, so timestep_ms is 0: one tick is one kinematic update, not a declared interval of simulated time
vision observations and rendering are not served: the driver binds the state observation mode and cap.world.render.v1 is not bound; render() of the fake returns one placeholder pixel
snapshot and restore are not offered: RLBenchEnv exposes no get_state/set_state pair

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
